hints: Follow a wave from the vibration generator to an end of the string, then consider what happens at that end.
Name the two waves that overlap after reflection.
walkthrough: The vibration generator sends a progressive wave along the string.
At a fixed end of the string, the wave is reflected and travels back along the string.
The incident and reflected waves travel in opposite directions and superpose, forming the stationary wave.

ai_rubric.observable: States that a wave travelling along the string is reflected at an end or fixed point.
States that the incident and reflected waves superpose.

hints: Use the nodes in the diagram to split the string into adjacent node-to-node sections.
Each adjacent node-to-node section is half a wavelength.
walkthrough: The 1.2 m string contains three adjacent node-to-node sections in the stationary-wave pattern.

ai_rubric.observable: Obtains a stationary-wave wavelength of 0.80 m.

hints: Express 0.24 s as a number of periods using T = 0.16 s.
After an extra half-period, every non-node point has the opposite displacement while the nodes remain fixed.
walkthrough: 0.24 s = 1.5T, which is one full period plus a further half-period.
After one full period the original profile is restored; the further half-period reverses the displacement of every non-node point.
Sketch the original stationary-wave shape reflected in the dashed line, with the same wavelength and amplitude and passing through the original nodes.

ai_rubric.observable: Sketch has the original wavelength throughout and passes through the intersections of the solid and dashed lines.
Sketch is reflected in the dashed line and has the same amplitude as the original wave.

hints: Use the stationary-wave loops, rather than the drawn displacement of the points at this instant.
Points in adjacent loops oscillate in antiphase.
walkthrough: The stationary-wave pattern places R and T in adjacent loops separated by a node.
All points in one loop oscillate in phase, while points in adjacent loops oscillate in antiphase.
Antiphase oscillations have a phase difference of 180°.
Therefore the phase difference between R and T is 180°.

hints: Use the wavelength from part (b) and the period given in part (c).
Use v = fλ with f = 1 / T, or use the equivalent form v = λ / T.
walkthrough: The wave equation is v = fλ and f = 1 / T, so v = λ / T.
Therefore the progressive-wave speed is 5.0 m s⁻¹.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses v = fλ with f = 1 / T, or equivalently v = λ / T.
Uses λ = 0.80 m and T = 0.16 s, or f = 6.25 Hz, to obtain 5.0 m s⁻¹.
